title: Private VPC preflight gatekeeper: Terraform checks for quotas, IAM, DNS, GPUs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a deterministic, idempotent preflight 'gatekeeper' that runs before any Private (VPC/on-prem) install or upgrade. The gatekeeper will execute a set of Terraform-friendly validation checks and emit structured results used by the installer and CI. It must validate cloud quotas (vCPU, GPUs, elastic IPs), IAM roles & policy bindings, DNS/private zone delegation, VPC/subnet capacity, and node-level GPU availability. The goal is to fail fast with actionable remediation steps so installs/rollouts do not hit capacity or permission errors in production environments.
tasks: Design gatekeeper interface: terraform plan/validate hook + standalone CLI that accepts a JSON manifest of cluster topology
Implement quota checks: query cloud provider APIs for vCPU, GCE/EC2 GPU SKUs, regional GPU availability, and reserved instance limits
Add IAM validation: verify service account roles, KMS key grants, and assume-role policies required by installer
DNS checks: ensure delegated private zone exists, correct NS records, and resolvers from target VPC can resolve installer control plane hostnames
Network checks: validate subnet CIDR capacity, route table attachments, and presence of required NAT/GW/IGW resources
Terraform integration: expose checks as a data source and a provider-friendly preflight module that returns structured pass/fail reasons
CI gating: wire preflight into ci/preflight-checks pipeline; make failures block merge to release branches
Acceptance tests: Terratest/Kitchen tests that mock quotas and return deterministic pass/fail scenarios
Documentation & runbook: Confluence runbook and Slack alerting path for remediation
Add telemetry: emit metric events for failures (quota, iam, dns, gpu) to the Console and create alerting rules
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper runs as part of the 'installer apply' flow and fails early with a concise JSON report when checks don't pass
Terraform module returns a stable output object with 'status' and 'reasons' that installer can use to stop or continue rollout
CI job ci/preflight-checks exists and blocks merges that would introduce failing preflight regressions
At least three cloud-providerquota scenarios covered by automated tests: sufficient, near-limit, exhausted
Documentation: Confluence page with step-by-step remediation for top 5 error codes and a one-page runbook for on-call
Observed false-positive rate < 5% across manual validation runs during pilot installs
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Infra, Installer, and Security. Agreed scope: cloud quotas, IAM, DNS, network, GPU SKU availability. Action: Ava to draft design doc.
2026-02-18: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Gatekeeper+Design. Decided to surface results as JSON and as human-friendly text. Use provider SDKs for quota queries.

2026-02-25: Spike complete. Prototype CLI (go) that queries AWS Service Quotas and GCE quotas; discovers GPU SKUs via DescribeInstanceTypes/ListAcceleratorTypes. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/preflight-gatekeeper/pull/3
2026-03-03: Terraform module v0.1 implemented to call external data source. POC integrated into private-installer repo; created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-installer/pull/291

2026-03-10: Determined trade-off: to avoid long cloud API latency, caching at CI level for quota snapshots is acceptable for merges, but live checks required for production installs. Added cache TTL and forced live mode for 'installer apply'.

2026-03-14: Implemented initial IAM validator (checks for kms:Decrypt, iam:PassRole for installer SA). Open PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/preflight-gatekeeper/pull/12. Marked blockers: DNS validation for cross-account private hosted zones needs additional permissions from networking team.
notes: Trade-off: live quota checks add install latency. Mitigation: short timeout (10s) + early UX so operators can run asynchronous preflight reports before apply.
GPU availability: cloud APIs can report SKU support but not real-time stock. We'll surface a 'probable' status and recommend alternate SKUs or burst fallback policies in Dedicated mode.
Terraform provider approach chosen for ease of consumption by existing installer stacks. Avoids requiring installers to embed Go code directly.
Security: gatekeeper will not store secret material. KMS checks use HEAD/iam simulation calls only; any elevated permissions require documented override and audit.
Operational: failures should map to runbook IDs so oncall can quickly determine remediation steps and which team to page
